
{{alias}}( [dtype][, options] )
    Returns a three-dimensional ndarray.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dtype: string|DataType (optional)
        Underlying data type. Default: 'float64'.

    options: Object (optional)
        Options.

    options.order: string (optional)
        Specifies whether an array is row-major (C-style) or column-major
        (Fortran-style). Default: 'row-major'.

    options.mode: string (optional)
        Specifies how to handle indices which exceed array dimensions. If equal
        to 'throw', an ndarray instance throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance
        normalizes negative indices and throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        indices exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal to
        'clamp', an ndarray instance sets an index exceeding array dimensions
        to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. Default: 'throw'.

    options.submode: Array<string> (optional)
        Specifies how to handle subscripts which exceed array dimensions. If a
        mode for a corresponding dimension is equal to 'throw', an ndarray
        instance throws an error when a subscript exceeds array dimensions. If
        equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance normalizes negative
        subscripts and throws an error when a subscript exceeds array
        dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        subscripts exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal
        to 'clamp', an ndarray instance sets a subscript exceeding array
        dimensions to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. If the
        number of modes is less than the number of dimensions, an ndarray
        instance recycles modes using modulo arithmetic.

        Default: [ options.mode ].

    options.readonly: boolean (optional)
        Boolean indicating whether an array should be read-only. Default: false.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        A three-dimensional ndarray.

    Examples
    --------
    > var arr = {{alias}}()
    <ndarray>
    > var sh = {{alias:@stdlib/ndarray/shape}}( arr )
    [ 0, 0, 0 ]
    > arr = {{alias}}( 'float32' )
    <ndarray>


{{alias}}( shape[, dtype][, options] )
    Returns a three-dimensional ndarray having a specified shape.

    Parameters
    ----------
    shape: ArrayLikeObject<integer>
        Array shape. Must contain exactly three elements.

    dtype: string|DataType (optional)
        Underlying data type. Default: 'float64'.

    options: Object (optional)
        Options.

    options.order: string (optional)
        Specifies whether an array is row-major (C-style) or column-major
        (Fortran-style). Default: 'row-major'.

    options.mode: string (optional)
        Specifies how to handle indices which exceed array dimensions. If equal
        to 'throw', an ndarray instance throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance
        normalizes negative indices and throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        indices exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal to
        'clamp', an ndarray instance sets an index exceeding array dimensions
        to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. Default: 'throw'.

    options.submode: Array<string> (optional)
        Specifies how to handle subscripts which exceed array dimensions. If a
        mode for a corresponding dimension is equal to 'throw', an ndarray
        instance throws an error when a subscript exceeds array dimensions. If
        equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance normalizes negative
        subscripts and throws an error when a subscript exceeds array
        dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        subscripts exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal
        to 'clamp', an ndarray instance sets a subscript exceeding array
        dimensions to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. If the
        number of modes is less than the number of dimensions, an ndarray
        instance recycles modes using modulo arithmetic.

        Default: [ options.mode ].

    options.readonly: boolean (optional)
        Boolean indicating whether an array should be read-only. Default: false.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        A three-dimensional ndarray.

    Examples
    --------
    > var arr = {{alias}}( [ 1, 2, 2 ] )
    <ndarray>[ [ [ 0.0, 0.0 ], [ 0.0, 0.0 ] ] ]
    > arr = {{alias}}( [ 1, 2, 2 ], 'float32' )
    <ndarray>[ [ [ 0.0, 0.0 ], [ 0.0, 0.0 ] ] ]


{{alias}}( K, M, N[, dtype][, options] )
    Returns a three-dimensional ndarray having a specified shape.

    Parameters
    ----------
    K: integer
        Number of elements in the first dimension.

    M: integer
        Number of elements in the second dimension.

    N: integer
        Number of elements in the last dimension.

    dtype: string|DataType (optional)
        Underlying data type. Default: 'float64'.

    options: Object (optional)
        Options.

    options.order: string (optional)
        Specifies whether an array is row-major (C-style) or column-major
        (Fortran-style). Default: 'row-major'.

    options.mode: string (optional)
        Specifies how to handle indices which exceed array dimensions. If equal
        to 'throw', an ndarray instance throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance
        normalizes negative indices and throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        indices exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal to
        'clamp', an ndarray instance sets an index exceeding array dimensions
        to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. Default: 'throw'.

    options.submode: Array<string> (optional)
        Specifies how to handle subscripts which exceed array dimensions. If a
        mode for a corresponding dimension is equal to 'throw', an ndarray
        instance throws an error when a subscript exceeds array dimensions. If
        equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance normalizes negative
        subscripts and throws an error when a subscript exceeds array
        dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        subscripts exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal
        to 'clamp', an ndarray instance sets a subscript exceeding array
        dimensions to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. If the
        number of modes is less than the number of dimensions, an ndarray
        instance recycles modes using modulo arithmetic.

        Default: [ options.mode ].

    options.readonly: boolean (optional)
        Boolean indicating whether an array should be read-only. Default: false.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        A three-dimensional ndarray.

    Examples
    --------
    > var arr = {{alias}}( 1, 2, 2 )
    <ndarray>[ [ [ 0.0, 0.0 ], [ 0.0, 0.0 ] ] ]
    > arr = {{alias}}( 1, 2, 2, 'float32' )
    <ndarray>[ [ [ 0.0, 0.0 ], [ 0.0, 0.0 ] ] ]


{{alias}}( obj[, dtype][, options] )
    Creates a three-dimensional ndarray from an array-like object or iterable.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obj: Object
        Array-like object or iterable from which to generate an ndarray. If an
        array-like object, the value must be a doubly nested array (i.e., an
        array-like object of array-like objects of array-like objects), where
        the nested arrays at each depth must have the same number of elements.
        If an iterable, the iterable must return nested array-like objects, each
        of which must have the same number of elements.

    dtype: string|DataType (optional)
        Underlying data type. Default: 'float64'.

    options: Object (optional)
        Options.

    options.order: string (optional)
        Specifies whether an array is row-major (C-style) or column-major
        (Fortran-style). Default: 'row-major'.

    options.mode: string (optional)
        Specifies how to handle indices which exceed array dimensions. If equal
        to 'throw', an ndarray instance throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance
        normalizes negative indices and throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        indices exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal to
        'clamp', an ndarray instance sets an index exceeding array dimensions
        to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. Default: 'throw'.

    options.submode: Array<string> (optional)
        Specifies how to handle subscripts which exceed array dimensions. If a
        mode for a corresponding dimension is equal to 'throw', an ndarray
        instance throws an error when a subscript exceeds array dimensions. If
        equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance normalizes negative
        subscripts and throws an error when a subscript exceeds array
        dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        subscripts exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal
        to 'clamp', an ndarray instance sets a subscript exceeding array
        dimensions to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. If the
        number of modes is less than the number of dimensions, an ndarray
        instance recycles modes using modulo arithmetic.

        Default: [ options.mode ].

    options.readonly: boolean (optional)
        Boolean indicating whether an array should be read-only. Default: false.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        A three-dimensional ndarray.

    Examples
    --------
    > var v = [ [ [ 1.0, 2.0 ], [ 3.0, 4.0 ] ] ];
    > var arr = {{alias}}( v, 'float32' )
    <ndarray>[ [ [ 1.0, 2.0 ], [ 3.0, 4.0 ] ] ]


{{alias}}( buffer[, byteOffset[, shape]][, dtype][, options] )
    Returns a three-dimensional ndarray view of an ArrayBuffer.

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer: ArrayBuffer
        Underlying ArrayBuffer.

    byteOffset: integer (optional)
        Integer byte offset specifying the location of the first indexed
        element. Default: 0.

    shape: ArrayLikeObject<integer> (optional)
        Array shape. Must contain exactly three elements. If not provided, the
        view spans from the byteOffset to the end of the underlying ArrayBuffer
        and the first two dimensions of the returned ndarray each have a size of
        one.

    dtype: string|DataType (optional)
        Underlying data type. Default: 'float64'.

    options: Object (optional)
        Options.

    options.order: string (optional)
        Specifies whether an array is row-major (C-style) or column-major
        (Fortran-style). Default: 'row-major'.

    options.mode: string (optional)
        Specifies how to handle indices which exceed array dimensions. If equal
        to 'throw', an ndarray instance throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance
        normalizes negative indices and throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        indices exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal to
        'clamp', an ndarray instance sets an index exceeding array dimensions
        to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. Default: 'throw'.

    options.submode: Array<string> (optional)
        Specifies how to handle subscripts which exceed array dimensions. If a
        mode for a corresponding dimension is equal to 'throw', an ndarray
        instance throws an error when a subscript exceeds array dimensions. If
        equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance normalizes negative
        subscripts and throws an error when a subscript exceeds array
        dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        subscripts exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal
        to 'clamp', an ndarray instance sets a subscript exceeding array
        dimensions to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. If the
        number of modes is less than the number of dimensions, an ndarray
        instance recycles modes using modulo arithmetic.

        Default: [ options.mode ].

    options.readonly: boolean (optional)
        Boolean indicating whether an array should be read-only. Default: false.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        A three-dimensional ndarray.

    Examples
    --------
    > var buf = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/buffer}}( 32 );
    > var arr = {{alias}}( buf, 0, [ 1, 2, 2 ], 'float32' )
    <ndarray>


{{alias}}( buffer[, byteOffset[, K, M, N]][, dtype][, options] )
    Returns a three-dimensional ndarray view of an ArrayBuffer.

    If `K`, `M`, and `N` are not provided, the returned ndarray view spans from
    the byteOffset to the end of the underlying ArrayBuffer.

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer: ArrayBuffer
        Underlying ArrayBuffer.

    byteOffset: integer (optional)
        Integer byte offset specifying the location of the first indexed
        element. Default: 0.

    K: integer (optional)
        Number of elements in the first dimension.

    M: integer (optional)
        Number of elements in the second dimension.

    N: integer (optional)
        Number of elements in the last dimension.

    dtype: string|DataType (optional)
        Underlying data type. Default: 'float64'.

    options: Object (optional)
        Options.

    options.order: string (optional)
        Specifies whether an array is row-major (C-style) or column-major
        (Fortran-style). Default: 'row-major'.

    options.mode: string (optional)
        Specifies how to handle indices which exceed array dimensions. If equal
        to 'throw', an ndarray instance throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance
        normalizes negative indices and throws an error when an index exceeds
        array dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        indices exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal to
        'clamp', an ndarray instance sets an index exceeding array dimensions
        to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. Default: 'throw'.

    options.submode: Array<string> (optional)
        Specifies how to handle subscripts which exceed array dimensions. If a
        mode for a corresponding dimension is equal to 'throw', an ndarray
        instance throws an error when a subscript exceeds array dimensions. If
        equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance normalizes negative
        subscripts and throws an error when a subscript exceeds array
        dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        subscripts exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal
        to 'clamp', an ndarray instance sets a subscript exceeding array
        dimensions to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. If the
        number of modes is less than the number of dimensions, an ndarray
        instance recycles modes using modulo arithmetic.

        Default: [ options.mode ].

    options.readonly: boolean (optional)
        Boolean indicating whether an array should be read-only. Default: false.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        A three-dimensional ndarray.

    Examples
    --------
    > var buf = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/buffer}}( 32 );
    > var arr = {{alias}}( buf, 0, 1, 2, 2, 'float32' )
    <ndarray>


{{alias}}.factory( dtype[, options] )
    Returns a function for creating a three-dimensional ndarray.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dtype: string|DataType
        Underlying data type.

    options: Object (optional)
        Options.

    options.order: string (optional)
        Specifies whether the default memory layout should be row-major (C-
        style) or column-major (Fortran-style). Default: 'row-major'.

    options.mode: string (optional)
        Specifies the default behavior when handling indices which exceed array
        dimensions. If equal to 'throw', an ndarray instance throws an error
        when an index exceeds array dimensions. If equal to 'normalize', an
        ndarray instance normalizes negative indices and throws an error when an
        index exceeds array dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance
        wraps around indices exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic.
        If equal to 'clamp', an ndarray instance sets an index exceeding array
        dimensions to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. Default:
        'throw'.

    options.submode: Array<string> (optional)
        Specifies how to handle subscripts which exceed array dimensions. If a
        mode for a corresponding dimension is equal to 'throw', an ndarray
        instance throws an error when a subscript exceeds array dimensions. If
        equal to 'normalize', an ndarray instance normalizes negative
        subscripts and throws an error when a subscript exceeds array
        dimensions. If equal to 'wrap', an ndarray instance wraps around
        subscripts exceeding array dimensions using modulo arithmetic. If equal
        to 'clamp', an ndarray instance sets a subscript exceeding array
        dimensions to either `0` (minimum index) or the maximum index. If the
        number of modes is less than the number of dimensions, an ndarray
        instance recycles modes using modulo arithmetic.

        Default: [ options.mode ].

    options.readonly: boolean (optional)
        Boolean indicating whether an array should be read-only by default.
        Default: false.

    Returns
    -------
    fcn: Function
        Function for creating a three-dimensional ndarray.

    Examples
    --------
    > var f = {{alias}}.factory( 'float32' );
    > var arr = f( [ 1, 2, 2 ] )
    <ndarray>[ [ [ 0.0, 0.0 ], [ 0.0, 0.0 ] ] ]

    See Also
    --------
